To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hormonal control of hepatic glycogen metabolism in the chick embryo is different from that in the chick and the rat.
glucagon and adrenaline activate hepatic glycogen breakdown in the chick embryo and that insulin does not inhibit this response.

the regulation of glycogenolysis by glucagon, adrenaline and insulin in chick embryo hepatocytes is similar to that in the adult chick, but that the Ca2+-dependent mechanisms that regulate glycogenolysis are absent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hormonal regulation of glycogen synthesis in chick embryo hepatocytes in vitro.
the regulation of carbohydrate metabolism in chick embryo liver.
the regulation of hepatic glycogen metabolism during the transition from embryonic to neonatal life, with special reference to the role of glucagon and insulin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in contrast with rat liver, the control of glycogenolysis in chick embryo liver appears to be independent of changes in intracellular free Ca2+.
the hormonal regulation of glycogen breakdown in chick embryo hepatocytes is different from that observed in the hepatocytes of the adult chicken.
glucagon and adrenaline are potent activators of glycogenolysis in hepatocytes from chick embryos.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hormonal control of hepatic glycogenolysis is not fully developed until the chick has hatched.
glucagon and adrenaline activate chick embryo glycogenolysis through a cAMP-independent pathway and that insulin does not inhibit glucagon- or adrenaline-stimulated glycogenesis.
the hormonal regulation of glycogen breakdown in chick embryo hepatocytes is qualitatively similar but quantitatively different from that in the adult chicken and in the rat.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of glycogenolysis is different in chick embryo and adult chicken liver.
, although the hormonal regulation of glycogen breakdown in chick embryo hepatocytes is similar in many ways to that of the adult, there are also significant quantitative differences.
the hormonal regulation of glycogen turnover in embryonic hepatocytes is qualitatively similar to that of the adult.
